newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF rejects Hanwa Bank objection to wind-up scheme.
newsitem.headline: MOF rejects Hanwa Bank objection to wind-up scheme.

text.p: Japan's Finance Ministry said on Monday it had rejected an objection filed last month by Hanwa Bank Ltd against a proposed scheme for liquidating the failed bank.
The ministry last year suspended operations at the second-tier regional bank, except for deposit withdrawals, as Hanwa was unable to recover bad loans.
Hanwa filed an objection with MOF in January and bank sources had cited unresolved issues regarding guarantees of job security for the bank's 850 employees.
Although a MOF official told a news conference that the ministry was doing its utmost to safeguard the employees' jobs, he said it found no reasons to justify Hanwa's objection.
He reiterated that the ministry's inspection of Hanwa showed that the bank's liabilities exceeded its assets and that the suspension was unavoidable.

The official also said MOF had recommended various measures to Hanwa over the years to improve its management and rejected the bank's charge that the ministry had abandoned its responsibility as the overseeing authority to help out the bank.
